problems.title: Under pressure (10 points).
problems.statement:
Magnetic fields in the Sun are constantly shaping the structure of various different features in the Solar atmosphere. Inside any feature, the magnetic field ($B$) adds to the total pressure exerted by the gas. This so-called magnetic pressure is a function of the height z and can be expressed as:

$$P_{mag}(z) = \frac{B^2(z)}{2\mu_0}$$

On the other hand, the gas can be considered to be in hydrostatic equilibrium and hence the gas pressure decays exponentially from an initial pressure value $P_0$ with increasing z. It can be expressed as,

$$P_{gas}(z) = P_0 e^{-z/H}$$

where H is the scale height, i.e. the height at which the pressure falls to $\frac{P_0}{e}$.
Consider one type of feature, a magnetic flux tube rising from the Solar surface up into an unmagnetized environment (see Figure below). Assuming that the total pressure of the material inside the tube and of the material outside it is in equilibrium,

figures.alt: Diagram of the solar atmosphere with a magnetic flux tube rising from the surface of the Sun; labels: Solar atmosphere, B (arrows fanning out at the top of the tube), Magnetic flux tube, Surface of the Sun.

parts.statement: Find an expression for the magnetic field strength as a function of height $z$.

answer.note: Inside the tube the gas pressure is negligible in the unmagnetized environment balance; total pressure equilibrium gives B^2(z)/(2μ0) = P0 e^{-z/H}.

parts.statement: If the magnetic field at the base of a flux tube is $0.3T$, and scale height $H$ in a given solar model is $150\ km$, at what height will the magnetic field be reduced to $0.03T$?
